the write counterpart of the string-named p2readGSPrivRegister: the same register-number switch (PMODE..SIGLBLID), storing the shadow copy to the memory-mapped GS register; the GS interrupt handler writes IMR through it

copies every renderer counter (vertices, primitives, texture loads, DMA, lighting and frame-time statistics) into the caller's block and resets the frame-time min/max; called from igPsx2VisualContext's statistics slot. Alternative p2ReadStatistics
stores the mode p2SendGifTags turns into points (0), lines (1) or filled primitives; igPsx2VisualContext slot 239 maps its argument 0/1/2 to 2/1/0
registered by AddIntcHandler(0, ...) (INTC_GS); reads CSR, dispatches finish, vsync and signal to p2FinishHandler/p2VsyncHandler/p2GsSignalHandler, masks and unmasks IMR, ends with sync/ei
registers p2GsInterruptHandler with AddIntcHandler and EnableIntc(INTC_GS) and builds the GS-register VIF templates
fills the table p2UploadGsRegisters reads per register index (DAT 0x56ae50) with the GS register addresses 0x00..0x7f
sends `count` register images of the current set as GIF A+D writes through the GS-register VU program (or the direct path for other programs); p2SendGsRegister sends one
reads CSR and printf's its ID and REV bytes; called once from p2InitGsInterrupt on the first open
stores the flag and marks the lights and VU buffers dirty; igPsx2VisualContext's slot setting _materialSpecularState calls it with the same value

called with the same mask just before p2SendRenderState: counts lights, looks up the state cache, rebuilds the vertex format, function tables and lighting functions the send then uploads. Alternative p2UpdateRenderState

only caller p2InitVuPrograms: clears every p2VariantsBitN table, points p2VariantSlots at them, fills them with p2FindVuProgramVariants per feature bit, then groups multi-feature programs into variant tables by bit count
walks a variant-table list for the table whose feature mask equals the program's
allocates a variant table for a program: one entry per combination of its feature bits' settings, all -1
frees every variant table of the six lists and clears them; called from p2CloseDisplay

for each variant table whose features the vertex array mask holds, combines its features' slot indexes, and when the table has that program points the low feature's slot at it and clears the other features from the mask
stores the mode in p2TextureCombineMode[program] and its nibble of the packed per-program word, marking the vertex format and function tables dirty
returns the u16 at +62 of a texture record, which p2LoadTexture fills from its height argument; p2Clear/p2SetScissor/p2SetViewport use it for the render target's height
pops a record from p2FreeTextures (growing the pool) and clears it; p2LoadTexture's first call
clears a record and pushes it back on p2FreeTextures
resets the texture free list and slots, creates the VRAM block list head from the texture base, registers the textureLoaded/textureDeferred predicate names and sets the default TEXA
DMA completion: a record waiting on the upload (state 4) whose VIF1 sequence has completed becomes state 5
DMA completion p2UploadTextures attaches to each GIF upload: state 2 becomes 3 (resident)
binds a texture: its palette through p2SetClut, else its TEX0 (address from the display buffer for buffer textures) into the current context's TEX0 and marks it dirty
stores the 2-bit texture function of the current program in the packed per-program word
sets TEX0.TFX of the current context and p2TextureFunction[program]
as p2SetTextureFunction, also setting TEX0.TCC (texture alpha) from its second argument
writes CLAMP_1/CLAMP_2 (WMS, WMT, MINU, MAXU, MINV, MAXV) of the current context and marks TEX0/CLAMP dirty
writes TEX1 MMAG/MMIN of the current context, clearing MXL for the non-mipmapped filters
writes TEX1 LCM, L and K of the current context
writes TEXA TA0, TA1 and AEM; p2InitTextures sets (0, 0x80, 0)
GIF image transfers (BITBLTBUF/TRXPOS/TRXREG/TRXDIR then IMAGE packets) of each texture record in a list, attaching p2TextureLoadDone to each
local-to-local GS transfer of a rectangle between two texture records, allocating both first
points FRAME/ZBUF/XYOFFSET at a colour (and optional depth) texture, saving the display's registers the first time
restores the FRAME/ZBUF/XYOFFSET p2SetRenderTarget saved and clears the targets
splits and merges the VRAM block list so the record occupies the found address range, freeing the records it covers
walks the VRAM block list for free or done blocks that fit the record's size and alignment, returning the block and address
finds VRAM space for a record (waiting on in-flight uploads if needed), places it and marks it state 2; returns whether it got space
marks a record, its palette and its chained records as in use until the current VIF1 packet completes (state 4 with p2TextureUploadDone)
appends a record to another's chain (+32) and counts it
stores the palette record (+36) p2FenceTexture fences with the texture
marks a loaded record (state != 1) for reload (state 6)
stores a new image pointer and marks the record for reload like p2InvalidateTexture
releases a record's VRAM block, waits for its upload, merges it with free neighbours and frees the record

DMA predicate p2AllocTextureMemory adds to the GIF channel: true once the recorded finished VIF1 sequence reaches its argument
finish function p2AllocTextureMemory queues with p2AddFinishFunc: keeps the newest finished VIF1 sequence (p2FinishFunc.sequence) that p2SequenceFinishedPredicate tests
local-to-local GS transfer from the draw buffer (or the Z buffer when the last argument is set) into a texture record, the source row flipped by the buffer height. Alternative p2CopyScreenToTexture
returns the record's first doubleword, the GIF sequence p2UploadTextures stores; igPsx2VisualContext waits on it with p2WaitDmaSequence(2, ...)
sets the stage's bit in the stage mask p2FenceUsedTexture walks
when a resident record was drawn with, clears the flag and fences it and every texture of the marked stages (p2FenceTexture)
stores the mode p2AllocTextureMemory tests to wait for VRAM through the GS finish (1) or the DMA predicate
